title: 1957 AHSME Problem 40
statement: If the parabola \(y=-x^2+bx-8\) has its vertex on the \(x\)-axis, then \(b\) must be:

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text: a positive or a negative rational number

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text: a positive or a negative irrational number

solutions.text:
The vertex lies on the \(x\)-axis exactly when the quadratic has one repeated root. Its discriminant must satisfy \[ b^2-4(-1)(-8)=b^2-32=0. \] Hence \(b=\pm\sqrt{32}=\pm4\sqrt2,\) a positive or negative irrational number.

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: A parabola whose vertex lies on the \(x\)-axis has a repeated root
Set the discriminant of \(-x^2+bx-8=0\) equal to zero
